title: The Grothendieck bottom edge computed on an augmented resolution comparison
statement: Let $A,B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories and $C$ an abelian category, all equipped with bounded below derived categories. Let $F:A\to B$ and $G:B\to C$ be additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with $F$ sending injectives to $G$-acyclics. Let $X\in A$, let $I$ resolve $X$ and $J$ resolve $F(X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $\phi:J^\bullet\to F(I^\bullet)$ satisfy $\iota_J^0\phi^0=F(\iota_I^0)$. For every $n\in\mathbb N$, the canonical Grothendieck bottom edge [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps] is the composite $R^nG(F(X))\xrightarrow{\rho_J}H^n(GJ)\xrightarrow{H^n(G\phi)}H^n(GFI)\xrightarrow{\rho_I^{-1}}R^n(GF)(X)$, where $\rho$ denotes the canonical right-derived resolution comparison [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. No Ext or sheaf cohomology comparison is involved.

proof.text: Extend I and J by zero. The augmentation J <- F(X)[0] is a quasi-isomorphism. The supplied degree-zero identity says that phi after this augmentation is the canonical map F(X)[0] -> F(I). Cancelling the augmentation in the derived category determines the represented map independently of phi. Use the canonical resolution comparison to identify F(I) with RF(X).

Identify F(X)[0] with the bottom truncation of RF(X) using left exactness and the canonical R^0F comparison. Under the truncation/shift identification defining grothendieckSpectralObjectHIso at q=0, the preceding map is the bottom-interval inclusion. Applying RG and H^n therefore gives the canonical grothendieckBottomEdgeMap.

The derived G units are invertible on J (injective terms) and F(I) (G-acyclic terms). Naturality of this unit along phi identifies the induced map with H^n(G phi). The composite derived comparison transports the target unit, and the ordinary resolution comparison transports the source unit. Cancelling the extension/homology comparisons gives rho_J followed by H^n(G phi) followed by rho_I inverse, in this order.
